props.gloss_en: a blind man is pores et shema [leads the Shema and its blessings]
R' Yehuda: whoever has not seen the luminaries in his days is not pores al shema
many have contemplated expounding the Chariot and never in their lives saw it
there [the Chariot] the matter depends on the understanding of the heart, and he concentrates and knows
here [the luminaries] it is because of benefit
and he [the blind man] has no benefit
and the Rabbanan: he does have benefit, as R' Yosei
R' Yosei: all my days I was troubled by this verse, 'and you shall grope at noon as the blind man gropes in darkness' (Deut 28:29) -- what does it matter to a blind man whether it is dark or light?

until an incident came my way: once I was walking in the dead of night and darkness, and I saw a blind man walking on the road with a torch in his hand; I said to him: my son, why do you need this torch?
the blind man: as long as the torch is in my hand, people see me and save me from the pits, the thorns and the briars
